sermon.title: Waiting 03/24/2019
sermon.speaker: Michael Silla
sermon.summary: A message on waiting on God and watching. Samaria’s famine, Saul’s impatience before Samuel came, and the disciples sleeping in Gethsemane show what happens when we give in to pressure. God calls His people to be watchmen, to rise and warn, and to wait for His timing.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: He says the king went after “Elijah the prophet” (6:15); in 2 Kings 6 it is Elisha. His words kept. Graphic Bible account (mothers eating a child, 2 Kings 6:28-29) kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What temptation does a Christian face?
chunks.short_answer: The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak; for a Christian the temptation is not to pursue God and righteousness.
chunks.text: The spirit is willing and the flesh is weak temptation if you’re not a Christian there’s temptation to sin sin will take you to hell if you are a Christian there is a temptation not to pursue God and righteousness. If. You are a Christian and you’re pursuing right there is a temptation to fall asleep. And. Not warn people of the coming judgement. And there’s more temptations there’s temptations all over right there’s all kinds of things. And so Jesus comes a second time he went and prayed he went away and prayed again and he count he found them asleep again for their eyes.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And He came and found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy. So He left them, went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words. Then He came to His disciples and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us be going. See, My betrayer is at hand.”

faqs.question: Is this story shocking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we should be shocked.

faqs.question: Was God judging Israel?
faqs.answer: Yes, he says God was judging that nation.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Jonathan attacked the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Then Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!” Now all Israel heard it said that Saul had attacked a garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel had also become an abomination to the Philistines. And the people were called together to Saul at Gilgal.

faqs.question: Did Saul experience God?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Spirit came on him.

faqs.question: Did Jesus need watchers?
faqs.answer: No; He wanted them to watch with Him.

faqs.question: Did the disciples make mistakes?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they decided to watch.
